newsitem.title: USA: Survey - 44 pct definitely won't vote for Dole.
newsitem.headline: Survey - 44 pct definitely won't vote for Dole.

text.p: Less than five weeks before Election Day, 44 percent of voters have definitely decided not to vote for Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, a new survey reported on Thursday.
Democratic President Bill Clinton holds a 16-point lead over Dole and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, according to a survey of 1,517 registered voters by the Washington-based Pew Research Group.
But Clinton's supporters are not overly enthusiastic, giving the president a grade of "C" for his White House performance so far, the survey found.
"American voters are modest in their enthusiasm for Bill Clinton, except in comparison to his Republican and Reform party rivals," a statement accompanying the survey said.
An "ominously high" 44 percent of those surveyed said they have decided not to vote for Dole and only 16 percent have said they might vote for Dole.
"Dislike of Clinton continues to be the dominant motive for supporting the former Senate Majority Leader," the survey found.

Clinton has been more successful in making a media impression, with 47 percent saying they hear more about Clinton, compared with the 31 percent who say they are hearing more about Dole in the news media.

The survey statement suggested Dole's failure to make an impact in the media may relate to rising public confidence in the economy: 55 percent rated their own financial situation excellent or good, up from 49 percent in 1994 and 42 percent in 1992.

Another indicator of voter sentiment, a poll taken in late September and released on Thusday by the Harris organisation, found that Clinton leads on such issues as the environment, education, health care and jobs by wide margins.
Even on crime and taxes, two traditionally Republican issues, Clinton leads by seven points and six points respectively.
On foreign policy and drugs, Clinton and Dole are virtually tied, the Harris Poll of 996 likely voters found.
The Harris Poll had a margin of error of three percentage points.
